questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The choice of study destination was based on a strong personal interest in Italian culture and a desire to experience a study environment that is very different from my home country. At the same time, the university’s course offerings closely matched the areas I wanted to deepen my knowledge in, particularly within finance and ESG-related topics, and the opportunity to gain an international perspective was an important factor in my decision.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall, it was relatively easy to find the necessary information upon arrival, as the university provided clear guidance and was helpful when questions arose. However, the university’s housing system did not function well in my case, which meant that accommodation arrangements were largely left to be handled independently upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival, I received assistance mainly through pre-arrival emails and an orientation meeting, including a welcome week for exchange students. The international office was also very supportive and responsive, providing helpful guidance with administrative and practical matters.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding off-campus housing in Venice was challenging, particularly on the island itself, where availability is limited and demand is high. It is generally easier to find accommodation on the mainland, which was an option we considered, but we were determined to live on the island. My main recommendation is to contact as many listings as possible and to view properties in person when feasible. In the end, we found accommodation through short-term rental platforms.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Future exchange students should be aware that the quality of off-campus housing can vary significantly and that rental prices are relatively high, especially on the island. However, despite these challenges, living on the island offers a unique experience that many will find worthwhile.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Initially, I accepted an off-campus housing offer but did not receive any further communication. In hindsight, this turned out positively, as the accommodation was located on the mainland, and I ultimately found housing on the island instead. I am very grateful to have had the opportunity to live on the island, as it greatly enhanced my overall exchange experience.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process was somewhat technical. Although the host institution provided a fairly detailed guide, some steps were not entirely intuitive. However, the international office was very helpful, and with their support, the process was manageable and could be completed successfully.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration required adding the selected courses to a study plan, which had to be consistent with the pre-approved courses from my home university. After this, it was necessary to complete a number of evaluation forms before being eligible to register for exams. Exam registration could only be completed at the earliest two weeks prior to the exam date.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Support was mainly provided through informational emails, written guides, and direct assistance via email correspondence when specific questions arose.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Overall, the registration process was successful, and I was able to enrol in the classes I wanted. There was one instance where I was temporarily registered for an incorrect course, but this was resolved without major issues.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My main advice to future exchange students is to ask for clarification whenever they are unsure about any part of the registration process, as support staff are helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The exam format was very different from what I am used to; however, my overall learning outcome has been positive.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The exam level may be slightly lower than what I am accustomed to at my home institution, which appears to be related to the exam format and the block structure of the courses, where each course is taught over a relatively short period of time. In terms of content, however, the academic level was fairly standard.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at the host institution was somewhat more informal than at UCPH, particularly in relation to exams. Lectures were shorter but scheduled over more days. Aside from these differences, the overall teaching approach was quite similar to what I am used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Behavioral Finance, ESG Risk Management, Corporate Banking, Advanced Corporate Finance, and Sustainable Corporate Strategy

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Overall, most expenses were in line with my expectations.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A variety of cultural, athletic, and social activities were available for students. These included sports activities such as rowing, as well as student associations that organised social events, including informal gatherings such as spritz nights and similar activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Although I did not participate extensively in these activities, I believe there were several good opportunities for students to engage in cultural, athletic, and social events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend that visiting students explore what is happening on the island itself, as Venice regularly hosts cultural events. For example, we attended a traditional gondola race on the Grand Canal. In addition, I strongly recommend visiting nearby cities, as travelling by train from Venice is very easy. Popular and worthwhile destinations include Bologna, Florence, Verona, and Milan.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the local culture was somewhat mixed. Venice is a unique city where tourism plays a very dominant role, which can make it challenging to fully connect with local everyday life. However, I found that the Italian culture to be present in the everyday life there.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any specific cultural differences to be particularly challenging. However, it was sometimes difficult to connect with local students, and I experienced that everyday processes could be less structured than what I am used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I particularly appreciated the laid-back attitude and the expressive nature of Italian culture, as well as the strong emphasis on enjoying everyday life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be proactive and patient with administrative processes, as some procedures can be technical and less structured than at UCPH.

2. Start looking for housing early and be prepared for limited availability, especially if you wish to live on the island.

3. Take advantage of the location by exploring Venice itself and travelling to nearby cities, as this greatly enhances the overall exchange experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The administrative system can be somewhat confusing at first. It is important to note that students do not register directly for courses, but instead enrol on Moodle to access course instructions and materials, and only need to register for exams.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was living in Venice and experiencing everyday life in a unique cultural setting, having the opportunity to travel and explore different parts of Italy, and taking courses that closely matched my academic interests.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during the exchange was the high level of tourism, which sometimes made it difficult to fully engage with local everyday life and also made it more challenging to pick up the Italian language.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
